content.title: About
content.content: Cherry cobbler is a classic American dessert made of a sweet cherry filling topped with a flaky biscuit‑like crust. The tartness of the cherries balances the buttery, slightly sweet dough that turns golden and crisp when baked.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cobbler originated in the 19th‑century United States as a simple way to use seasonal berries.
A scoop of vanilla ice cream is a traditional accompaniment.
The topping can be a runny batter or a more solid biscuit dough, depending on the recipe.
Original recipes used whole‑wheat flour, but today many variations use whole‑grain or gluten‑free flours.
Cobbler is often baked in ceramic dishes, which retain heat and give the crust extra crunch.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Cherries contain anthocyanins that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Source of vitamin C
items.content: Cherry provides vitamin C, supporting immune function.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber from the fruit aids digestion and promotes satiety.

items.title: Low‑fat filling
items.content: Most of the calories come from the crust, while the fruit portion is relatively low in fat.

items.title: Cardiovascular support
items.content: Flavonoids in cherries may help lower blood pressure.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Traditional crusts contain wheat flour, which is unsuitable for people with celiac disease.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Recipes often call for a generous amount of sugar, increasing the dessert’s calorie load.

items.title: Acidity of cherries
items.content: Those with acid reflux may experience discomfort after eating cherry cobbler.

items.title: Undercooked dough
items.content: If the crust is not baked through, it can remain dense and harder to digest.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve cobbler warm, typically with a scoop of vanilla ice cream or a dollop of whipped cream. It can be eaten straight from the baking dish or sliced into individual portions.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Reheat in the oven before serving to restore the crisp crust.
